stories.title: XPENG sets a 2027 retail training timetable for its IRON humanoid
stories.summary: XPENG says IRON will begin training as a store assistant in early 2027, with a public release targeted for the second quarter.
paragraphs: XPENG presented its updated IRON humanoid at its November 25 AI Day in Guangzhou. The company also introduced Turing Physical AI Architecture, a framework it says connects perception, decisions and motion across its vehicles and robots.
XPENG plans to start training IRON in its own stores in the first quarter of 2027. It set a separate target for a public release in the second quarter. Both milestones are company targets.

stories.title: ROBOTERA reports humanoid deployments at 11 Guangdong postal hubs
stories.summary: The robot maker says its China Post deployment now spans eleven hubs in eight cities, following a pilot in Guangzhou.
paragraphs: ROBOTERA announced on November 17 that humanoid robots were deployed at eleven hubs run by China Post's Guangdong branch. The company traced the rollout to a March pilot in Guangzhou.
The work includes parcel induction, which feeds items into a sorting line. ROBOTERA disclosed the number of sites, while the number of robots at those sites remains undisclosed.

stories.title: Chengdu unveils a Gongga humanoid designed to replan household tasks
stories.summary: The fifth-generation Gongga is designed to remember where objects were, predict the results of a move, and revise its plan when its surroundings change.
paragraphs: The Chengdu Humanoid Robot Innovation Center unveiled its fifth-generation Gongga robot on November 11. Sichuan Online reports that the center designed its new control system for a household where people move things between tasks.

The center says Gongga combines color and depth cameras with information about its own position to update a 3D map. Its memory stores where objects were seen and what happened during earlier attempts. If an object is moved or a step fails, the robot can update its plan and use a model of the scene to predict the likely effects of its next move.
The reports describe the center's design and capability claims. They give no success rates across unfamiliar homes or timetable for consumer availability.

stories.title: Yongda Auto agrees to buy 400 UBTECH humanoids
stories.summary: The companies plan to use the U1 Pro for product demonstrations, sales promotion, and customer service, with delivery targeted by the end of 2026.
paragraphs: Chinese auto dealer Yongda Auto agreed to buy 400 U1 Pro humanoids under a partnership announced on November 11, according to The Paper. UBTECH is targeting delivery by year-end. The companies also plan to open a joint robot showroom in Shanghai.

Red Star News describes the full-body U1 Pro as a stationary robot designed for conversation. The proposed uses center on helping customers experience products and interacting with visitors at dealerships.
The coverage confirms the announced purchase and delivery target. It gives no confirmed count of units delivered to Yongda or final contract price.

stories.title: Beijing plans real-world tests for embodied AI robots
stories.summary: The city's 2026–2028 plan calls for a shared test site and aims to collect more than one million hours of robotics data across at least 100 real-world settings.
paragraphs: Beijing's municipal industry bureau issued its 2026–2028 action plan for embodied AI robots on November 11. The plan calls for a test site with several kinds of robots. Organizations that use robots would propose tasks, and teams building AI models would try to complete them under a common evaluation process.

Beijing aims to collect more than one million hours of data across at least 100 real-world settings. The plan also calls for pilots in manufacturing, warehousing, retail, and public services, plus a testing and certification system covering safety and reliability.
The policy took effect on November 11. The test site, data collection and application pilots are program goals through 2028.

stories.title: Joyson delivers its first robot compute backpack to Unitree
stories.summary: The add-on combines a computer and power system so robots can process sensor data and run AI models locally.
paragraphs: Joyson Electronics says its robotics subsidiary delivered a first compute backpack to Unitree on November 10. The external module includes a local computing platform and its own power system. Joyson says the design can work with Unitree's humanoid, four-legged, and wheeled robots.

The idea is to give a robot more room to process sensor inputs and run AI models on board. Joyson also says the companies are working on pilots for auto-parts production and other manufacturing tasks.
The announcement describes a first delivery. It gives no measured improvement in battery life or timetable for broader availability.

stories.title: AgiBot X2 robots take visitor-service roles in Chengdu
stories.summary: Three X2 humanoids serve visitors at Kuanzhai Alley, with roles spanning welcome desks, cultural interpretation, and retail.
paragraphs: AgiBot says it has partnered with Chengdu Culture & Tourism Group to deploy three X2 humanoids at Kuanzhai Alley. Their jobs include answering visitor questions, explaining local culture, and presenting and handing over retail products.

The company says the retail system uses a vision-language-action model, which connects what a robot sees and understands with its movements. It reports support for more than 20 product types, over 98% task success, and roughly 30 seconds per task.
Those performance figures come from AgiBot. The announcement does not establish how the system performs across other shops or how much supervision it needs.

stories.title: X2 joins a hospital reception desk with Ant Afu
stories.summary: AgiBot reports a hospital deployment that answers visitor questions and helps people navigate outpatient services.
paragraphs: AgiBot says an X2 humanoid integrated with Ant Afu is working at Peking University People's Hospital. It draws on hospital information to answer routine questions about departments, visits, and directions.

The announcement cites hospital operating figures through September 30: 46,686 interactions over 66 working days, averaging 707 a day. These are reported usage counts, rather than an independent evaluation of answer accuracy.
The deployment illustrates a public-service role for an embodied interface: helping visitors find information and their way around a busy building.

stories.title: AgiBot outlines a university robotics training program
stories.summary: The company plans more than 1,000 robots and software access for hands-on teaching and research at Chinese universities.
paragraphs: AgiBot says its university initiative will provide more than 1,000 robots across wheeled, humanoid, and quadruped platforms. The first group includes over 20 universities, with Peking, Tsinghua, and Zhejiang among those named.

The company values the hardware and software membership support at about RMB 200 million. Its AIMA tools are intended to connect classroom work with model training, algorithm development, and experiments on physical robots.
This is an announced education partnership. Equipment commitments should not be read as confirmation that every robot has already been delivered.

stories.title: Humanoid robots take the stage in Guangzhou
stories.summary: A National Day show puts coordinated humanoid performances and public interaction in the spotlight at the Guangdong Science Center.
paragraphs: China Youth Daily reports that a robot performance program premiered in Guangzhou on September 30, with public shows scheduled for October 1–7 at the Guangdong Science Center. Humanoid robots perform group choreography alongside human entertainers, with robot-dog interaction and audience participation also on the program.

The event brings robotics into a public cultural setting. Coordinated stage performances demonstrate a specific application; they do not establish that the robots can work autonomously across unrelated everyday tasks.

stories.title: AgiBot’s A3 gets a native NetEase Cloud Music integration
stories.summary: Voice-controlled music is scheduled to reach the full-size humanoid on October 15. Music-generated movement remains a development goal.
paragraphs: AgiBot says its A3 humanoid now integrates NetEase Cloud Music at the system level, connecting voice requests, music search, account authentication, and playback. The company plans to make voice song requests available from October 15, with account capabilities dependent on delivered software and authorization.

AgiBot reports pilot testing at Chimelong Spaceship park. Generating gestures from music, an AI DJ, and interactive singing are described as future development directions. Public or commercial music playback requires separate licensing; the pilot does not provide blanket commercial authorization.

stories.title: More than 300 robots join the everyday life of a theme park
stories.summary: AgiBot and Chimelong put robots to work across performances, visitor guidance, education, retail, and hospitality in Hengqin.
paragraphs: AgiBot’s September 28 announcement describes a September 24 launch at Chimelong Spaceship park in Hengqin. The company says more than 300 robots are regularly deployed across seven application areas, including entertainment, education, visitor guidance, retail, and hotel services.

The announcement also marks the delivery of AgiBot’s 20,000th robot, an A3 Ultra, to Chimelong. The partners launched a joint tourism-and-robotics research institute and announced a 5G-A robotics application with China Mobile.
These are company-reported deployment figures. The announcement does not provide an independent assessment of reliability, operating cost, or how much human supervision each application requires.

stories.title: Unitree releases its humanoid base model and fine-tuning code
stories.summary: The Chinese project README records a September 28 release of UnifoLM-WLA-1.0-Base and tools for adapting the model.
paragraphs: Unitree’s Chinese-language project README lists the September 28 release of UnifoLM-WLA-1.0-Base and fine-tuning code. It follows September releases of perception-model weights and code for training action experts.

Unitree describes UnifoLM-WLA-1.0 as a six-billion-parameter humanoid foundation model trained using approximately 2,500 hours of real-robot data, with a single model covering 64 tabletop and whole-body manipulation tasks. These task and training figures are the company’s reported results, rather than independent benchmarks reproduced by SuperRobots.

stories.title: A wheeled tennis robot meets Wang Qiang on court
stories.summary: LimX Dynamics and Enhance pair a TRON 2 mobile platform with a tennis-training system at the Billie Jean King Cup finals.
paragraphs: LimX Dynamics says the TENNIIX ULTRA MAX tennis-training robot appeared at the Billie Jean King Cup finals in Shenzhen and interacted on court with professional player Wang Qiang. The system combines Enhance’s TENNIIX PRO AI tennis technology with LimX’s TRON 2 wheeled-leg mobile platform.

The company describes ball tracking, changes in position, and adaptive ball delivery during the demonstration. Its proposed applications include clubs and youth coaching. The announcement documents a demonstration, rather than a quantified comparison with human training partners or evidence of broad commercial adoption.

stories.title: Unitree’s G1+ adds stronger joints and richer sensing
stories.summary: The upgraded humanoid brings a two-axis neck, stereo and wide-angle vision, touch sensing, and external power support.
paragraphs: Shangguan News, republished by Sina on September 22, reports that Unitree announced the G1+ on September 14. Unitree’s Chinese product page lists a two-degree-of-freedom neck, upgraded motors, stereo and wide-angle cameras, head touch sensing, external power support, and a six-microphone array.

The manufacturer lists the standard model at RMB 95,000 including tax. It states that specifications vary with configuration and usage, and that some demonstrated functions are still under development. The upgrades describe hardware and interaction capabilities, rather than a guarantee of general-purpose autonomy.

stories.title: D-Robotics raises $400 million for robot chips and development tools
stories.summary: The Series C round backs Sunrise chips and a software platform spanning data collection, training, simulation, and deployment.
paragraphs: Shenzhen News reports that D-Robotics announced a US$400 million Series C round on September 17, led by Mirae Asset with participation from Meituan and other investors. The company plans to expand its Sunrise chip portfolio and build software covering data collection, model training, simulation, and inference deployment.

The report says cumulative Sunrise chip shipments exceeded eight million. That figure concerns chips across the company’s product portfolio; it is not a count of humanoid robots. The funding supports the infrastructure used by robot developers, rather than a newly announced robot model.
